text: You're in Midtown, New York. It's one minute past noon.
The Sun went dark eight minutes ago. You can't know yet.
The whole sky switches off at once.
Its last light takes one more second to run out.
The stars were there all along.
Jupiter keeps glowing. It won't notice for an hour.
The air has no time to cool.
Then, the light that was five seconds late arrives.
